response.query: What concrete linkage algorithms and tuning parameters (Fellegi–Sunter weights, ML matchers), and which PPRL options should we adopt, and how will match probabilities be calibrated?
response.answer: Use the Fellegi-Sunter model for probabilistic record linkage, adjust weights based on field value frequencies, and calibrate match probabilities with EM algorithm.

results.title: A simple two-step procedure using the Fellegi–Sunter model for frequency-based record linkage - PMC
results.content: Matching weights are adjusted based on frequency distributions of the agreed field values among matches and non-matches, estimated by the Fellegi–Sunter model without relying on prior studies or training data. The magnitude of the weight for a specific field is dependent on two important sets of parameters: the probability of errors associated with the field values, and frequencies of agreed field values among truly matched record pairs. The true frequencies reflect the number of truly matched record pairs that agree on a specific field value. We propose to estimate the number of true matches (and number of true non-matches) that agree on values with different frequency levels by weighting the record pairs using the match probability derived based on the FS model. The number of true match record pairs agreeing on a field value with frequency *l*, denoted as , and the number of true non-match record pairs agreeing on a field value with frequency *l*, denoted as , are estimated by probability weighting as follows:. Record pairs agreeing on field values that are more frequent among true matches than among true non-matches receive a positive adjustment of the agreement weight, leading to a greater likelihood to be a match. The widely used FS model for probabilistic record linkage does not leverage information on the frequencies of field values and hence results in the same matching weights for record pairs agreeing on common values and those agreeing on rare values. Our approach utilizes the FS model to estimate the frequency distributions of the field values among true matches and among true non-matches for record pairs with field agreement without the need of training data. Although frequency-based weight adjustment can be similarly implemented after model parameters are estimated, there is little improvement in matching performance, seen by the negligible differences in AUC produced by weight adjustment in all three scenarios of the simulation study when the FS model parameters are set to equal to the true values (results not shown). In addition, our weight adjustment method is based on the assumption that the frequency distribution of agreed values of one field is independent of the agreement status of other fields given the true match status.

results.title: An Improved Fellegi-Sunter Framework for Probabilistic Record Linkage Between Large Data Sets - Marco Fortini, 2020
results.content: # An Improved Fellegi-Sunter Framework for Probabilistic Record Linkage Between Large Data Sets. Fellegi and Sunter propose an optimal statistical test in order to assign the match status to the candidate pairs, in which the needed parameters are obtained through EM algorithm directly applied to the set of candidate pairs, without recourse to training data. The present work proposes an efficient approach in which the comparison of records between lists are minimised while the EM estimates are modified by modelling tables with structural zeros in order to obtain unbiased estimates of the parameters. *Data matching: concepts and techniques for record linkage, entity resolution, and duplicate detection*. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society* B 39: 1–38. *Data quality and record linkage techniques*. “A Theory for Record Linkage”, *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 64, 328: 1183–1210. “Advances in Record-Linkage Methodology as Applied to Matching the 1985 Census of Tampa, Florida”. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 84: 414–420. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 96(453): 32–41. *Computational Statistics & Data Analysis*, *52*(1): 299–308. “Using the EM Algorithm for Weight Computation in the Fellegi-Sunter Model of Record Linkage”. *Proceedings of the Section on Survey Research Methods: American Statistical Association:* 667–671. “Overview of record linkage and current research directions”. “Improving EM Algorithm Estimates for Record Linkage Parameters”. #### Share this publication. #### Share access to this article. results.title: Estimating parameters for probabilistic linkage of privacy-preserved datasets - PMC
results.content: In this paper, we present a method for estimating the probabilities and threshold values for probabilistic privacy-preserved record linkage using Bloom filters. ### Results Linkage of the synthetic datasets using the estimated probabilities produced an F-measure that was comparable to the F-measure using calculated probabilities, even with up to 20% error. In this paper, we present a method for accurately estimating probabilities and an optimal threshold cut-off value that can be applied when using Bloom filters within the Fellegi-Sunter model for record linkage. In this paper, we evaluate our parameter estimation method in two ways: firstly, in a simulation study using synthetic datasets with varying degrees of error; and secondly, on three large-scale administrative datasets, comparing the resultant linkage quality against the quality achieved using calculated m- and u-probabilities. ### Estimating m and u probabilities The EM algorithm has been used to calculate the m-probabilities (**_m_**_)_, u-probabilities (**_u_**) and the proportion (**_p_**) of record pairs that match in probabilistic linkage [21]. Using the information generated during the EM step, we can estimate the quality of linkage for every combination of weights between a range of possible threshold values (i.e. using precision, recall and F-measure). These results show that the use of EM for probability estimation, combined with our threshold estimation technique, provided linkage quality comparable to the best achievable using calculated probabilities, on data with up to 20% error. F-measure at threshold estimate Open in a new tab In our simulation study, the use of the EM algorithm to estimate probabilities for a de-duplication linkage produced results comparable to those produced by calculated probabilities, even with synthetic datasets that contained 20% introduced error. The threshold values estimated in our study were consistently higher than the optimum threshold when using the calculated probabilities, with fewer false positives and more false negatives returned in each of the linkages (with the exception of the ‘perfect’ synthetic dataset). Provided the datasets being linked have sufficient matches, the estimation technique will produce optimal m-probabilities and a suitable threshold cut-off for the linkage. As we have shown, use of the EM algorithm and our threshold estimation technique provides a robust method of estimating parameters for probabilistic linkage of Bloom filter datasets.
